o: Per store with ≥ 3 products, find the priciest and cheapest products; report stores where the expensive item's stock is lower than the cheap item's stock, along with the ratio cheapest_qty / priciest_qty rounded to 2 decimals. Aggregate per store with GROUP BY, attach the extreme prices via a HAVING-filtered CTE, then pivot quantities with conditional aggregation.
k: Filter stores to ≥ 3 products early with HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3.
Conditional aggregation (MAX(CASE WHEN ...)) pivots the extreme-price rows into columns.
The imbalance condition is a HAVING comparison between the two aggregated quantities.

a.n: Approach 1: Grouped aggregation with conditional pivoting
a.i: First CTE computes per-store max/min price and product count (filtered to ≥ 3). Join back to inventory to tag each row as the max-price or min-price row, then group once more to extract product names and quantities, compute the ratio, and apply the imbalance condition in HAVING.
s: CTE agg: per store, MAX(price), MIN(price), COUNT(*) HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3.
Tag inventory rows joined to agg with is_max / is_min flags.
Final select: pivot product names and quantities with MAX(CASE ...), ratio = ROUND(min_qty / max_qty, 2).
HAVING min_qty > max_qty; ORDER BY ratio DESC, store_name ASC.

c.python:
WITH agg AS (
  SELECT store_id, MAX(price) AS max_p, MIN(price) AS min_p, COUNT(*) AS pcnt
  FROM inventory
  GROUP BY store_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
),
tagged AS (
  SELECT i.store_id, i.product_name, i.quantity,
         CASE WHEN i.price = a.max_p THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_max,
         CASE WHEN i.price = a.min_p THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_min
  FROM inventory i
  JOIN agg a ON a.store_id = i.store_id
)
SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, s.location,
       MAX(CASE WHEN t.is_max = 1 THEN t.product_name END) AS most_exp_product,
       MAX(CASE WHEN t.is_min = 1 THEN t.product_name END) AS cheapest_product,
       ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN t.is_min = 1 THEN t.quantity END) /
             MAX(CASE WHEN t.is_max = 1 THEN t.quantity END), 2) AS imbalance_ratio
FROM tagged t
JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = t.store_id
GROUP BY s.store_id, s.store_name, s.location
HAVING MAX(CASE WHEN t.is_min = 1 THEN t.quantity END) >
       MAX(CASE WHEN t.is_max = 1 THEN t.quantity END)
ORDER BY imbalance_ratio DESC, s.store_name ASC;

a.t: O(I log I) — grouping/joining over all inventory rows I

w: An alternative uses window functions (ROW_NUMBER per store ordered by price DESC/ASC) instead of the agg CTE — equally valid. Pitfalls: dividing before confirming the imbalance (division by zero if the pricey item has 0 stock — the HAVING guards this only if written on quantities, so keep the ratio in SELECT and the comparison in HAVING), and forgetting the ≥ 3 product filter which excludes Corner Shop and Plaza Store.
